note: The versions this project is supposed to cover, and the eras they belong to. tools/targets.py prints a verdict for each one: real Java (a JVM in the page), one layer away, or blocked by the runtime. Scope: every release and every snapshot, not a hand-picked list. Two rows answer for them, and the launcher says which one a version is on: the compiled row (smooth, mods baked at build time) and the real-JVM row (an unmodified client, Fabric at play time, not smooth). A version with no build on either row is listed as blocked, with the reason, rather than offered.

groups.name: Latest snapshot
groups.why: so a new version is never a surprise: the newest snapshot is always the hardest one, because it is the one nobody has ported

groups.name: The 26.x generation
groups.why: Java 25 and a renderer Mojang rewrites: compiled by the workspace engine for releases, and the wall for snapshots is the renderer, named in ports.json rather than hidden

groups.name: Legacy but modern enough
groups.why: modded servers, old worlds, the versions mods were written for

groups.name: Pre-release eras
groups.why: Indev, Alpha and Beta: tiny clients, everything they need is inside the jar

groups.name: The 1.21 line
groups.why: compiled from the official client, vanilla, with the mods path documented rather than pretended

groups.name: Uncovered middle (own engine needed)
groups.why: 1.16.5 - 1.20.4 has no licensed engine at all, and every snapshot of that era inherits the gap: this is the range the project's own TeaVM engine is for
